bands.note: RUB retail petrol 2018-2023 ranged 43-62. Floor 35 is the historic floor (2017-2018 lows ~35-38), kept BELOW 38.28 so a 38.28 L volume on a 2019 receipt reads as a plausible price and the pair abstains (receipt-025 is step-3 history territory, not a band call). High 100 leaves headroom over the ~62 peak without reaching the 2026+ level.

Retail petrol has not been under 40 since 2019; the corpus's own regional outlier is 450 (Crimean AI-100, 2026), so 500 leaves headroom. Round numbers on purpose - the band separates ~20 L from ~70-450 RUB/L, it does not price fuel.
RUB diesel tracks petrol closely (48.09 in 2020, 62.89 in 2024). Same floor/high as petrol for the era.
RUB diesel 2026 includes Crimean regional outliers (245, 259). Same wide band as petrol.

LPG runs roughly a third of petrol. The band deliberately overlaps LPG fill volumes (40-80 L), so an unmarked LPG pair - 52.15 X 23.99 on receipt-012 - has BOTH operands in band and abstains rather than swapping. A petrol band would reject 23.99 and call 52.15 the price; this is the row that makes the fuel-kind key load-bearing.

EUR/L retail ~1.30-2.00 across the eurozone in the corpus era. 1.0-3.0 is deliberately coarse: it only separates a litre price from a fill volume. The client keys on currency, not country, so a French or German receipt gets the same band.
EUR diesel ~1.75-1.92 in the corpus (Estonian Circle K). Same coarse band as petrol.
EUR LPG ~0.60-0.90, roughly a third of petrol, same relationship as RUB.
KZT/L retail ~200-300 in the corpus era. 100-1000 separates a 24.69 L volume from a 243 KZT price (receipt-033).
KZT diesel tracks KZT petrol. Same coarse band.
KZT LPG roughly a third of KZT petrol. Same family relationship as the other currencies.
